audit.why: Emerald+ 50.74% over 408 games. The full layer calls the matchup FAVOURED at 4/10 difficulty, which is a little generous against a coin-flip win rate, but the content layer's 'EVEN, win through teamfight' framing is the one the player reads and it is right.

Rumble takes levels 2-3, it evens from 4-5 as she buys HP, and she owns two items. Correct as written. She has exactly one gap-close (Arctic Assault, 18s at rank 1) and no dash otherwise, which is why the early window is real.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of the four spikes are built on a fabricated mechanic: 'her percent-HP W'. Winter's Wrath has no percent-health component.
audit.why: Riot's Winter's Wrath description in full: 'Sejuani swings her mace twice, dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks.' No max-health scaling, and the kit file carries no percentHealth flag on it. Her two-item spike is raw stat weight plus Frost Armor's free armour and magic resist, not percent-health damage. Telling a Rumble he cannot win a grind because of percent-HP damage that does not exist sends him to the wrong item build.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text and spikes[3].text rewritten around the real source of her scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the North grants Sejuani immunity to slows while Frost Armor holds. The matchup's stated win condition is 'double Electro-Harpoon to pin her' — and against a Sejuani who has been out of combat, that pin simply does not apply.
audit.why: Riot's passive description: after being out of combat Sejuani gains Frost Armor, which grants Armor and Magic Resist 'and immunity to slows', persisting for a short time after she takes damage. Every first engage of a wave starts with Frost Armor up. The correct sequencing is therefore: land a hit to break it, then Electro-Harpoon — throwing the harpoons first wastes both charges on a slow-immune target. Naming Arctic Assault (Q, 18s) as her gap-close also matters: the text twice calls Winter's Wrath her gap-close, which is wrong.
audit.corrected: Stated in wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], spikes[0].text, dosFull[0].d and the Key Ability Interactions report line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup repeatedly says to 'trade around her E cooldown' and 'engage once Permafrost is down'. Permafrost is on a 1.5 second cooldown — it is never down.
audit.why: Permafrost is gated on Frost stacks, not on its own cooldown: Riot's text is that it 'freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks'. Stacks come from Winter's Wrath (9/8/7/6/5s) and Glacial Prison. So the ability to track is Winter's Wrath, and the way to be safe from the stun is to not eat W swings, not to count down a stun cooldown that refreshes in a second and a half.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d rewritten to track Winter's Wrath at 9s and Arctic Assault at 18s instead.

edits.after: Full tank Sejuani with Frozen Heart and Thornmail simply outlasts Flamespitter's burn; it is her raw stat weight, not any percent-HP damage, that wins the grind — shift to Equalizer teamfight impact.
